text: Did the student fail the course because of something they intentionally did?
Was the failure due to the student missing an exam or assignment?
Was the student mistakenly enrolled in the wrong course or taking a course they weren't supposed to take?
Did the student fail because of a grading error or administrative mistake?
Did the student cheat or violate academic integrity rules in the course?
Was the failure caused by a physical or mental health problem of the student?
Did the student actually take and participate in the course's assessments?
Did the student fail because the course was designed or graded in a way that a normally excellent student would fail (e.g., strict relative grading, curve, or trick)?
Was the student unaware of a course requirement or rule that led to failing?
Was the student's failing caused by something outside their control, such as another person's action or an external event?
Was the course a physical education or sports course?
Was the student's failure caused by another person (not an external event like weather or accident)?
Did the student get a correct answer marked wrong, or their work mistakenly attributed to another person, due to another person's action?
Did another student or person sabotage or interfere with the student's work or exam?
Was the failure caused by a teacher/instructor's action or decision?
Was the student's failing caused by a family member or friend's action?
Was the other person who caused the failure a fellow student or classmate?
Did the classmate cause the student to fail by getting a higher relative grade, pushing the student below a cutoff?
Did the classmate copy the student's work, causing the student to be accused of or penalized for plagiarism/collusion?
Did the classmate cause the student to fail by distracting them, making noise, or disrupting the exam environment?
Did the classmate physically take or hide the student's exam or assignment?
Did the classmate cause the student's failure through the student's own mistake or misunderstanding caused by the classmate's words or actions?
Did the classmate physically harm or injure the student, preventing them from completing the course?
Was the failure due to the student being falsely accused of something by the classmate?
Did the classmate's action cause the student to miss an exam or deadline?
Was the student's failing related to the student's identity or enrollment records being altered by the classmate?
Did the classmate and the student submit identical work, and the classmate copied from the student, leading both to be penalized?
Was the course a driving course?
Did the classmate's action cause the student to be wrongly identified as the person who did something wrong?
Did the classmate impersonate the student on an exam or assignment?
Did the student's failure involve a misunderstanding where the classmate was in the same course and something about the classmate's situation directly affected the student's grade?
Did the classmate die, and did that death cause the student to fail the course?
Was the student's failing the result of a group project where the classmate's poor performance dragged down the student's grade?
Did the student have the option to choose their own group partners and willingly chose this classmate?
Did the classmate fail to contribute to the group project (e.g., did no work at all)?
Did the grading of the group project depend on the group's collective/aggregate result rather than individual contributions, so the classmate's lack of work caused the student to fail?
Was the course failed solely because of the group project component (i.e., the student would otherwise have passed on individual work)?
Did the student know in advance that the classmate would not contribute, yet still rely on them?
Did the student do all the group's work themselves, but the project still failed or was graded poorly because of the classmate's assigned part being missing or wrong?
Did the classmate promise to do their part but then failed to deliver, leaving the group project incomplete?
Was the group project's grading threshold such that even the student's own portion alone could not earn a passing overall mark?
Did the classmate's missing part cause the entire group project to be rejected or given zero?

Did the student complete and submit the group project, doing the classmate's part as well, and was it graded; yet the failure was because the classmate's assigned part was wrong or missing in a way the student did not fix?
Did the classmate actively do their part of the project but do it incorrectly, harming the group grade?
Was the group project submitted incomplete because the classmate never produced their assigned portion, and no one filled in that portion before submission?
Did the student do their own part correctly, but the project was graded as a whole and the classmate's uncompleted part left a gap that lowered the total score below passing?

Was the group project graded in a way where each member received the group's overall score, and the classmate's non-contribution meant the group's overall score was below passing, causing the student to fail despite good individual work?
Did the classmate do literally no work on the project at all?
Was the classmate assigned to the student's group by the instructor (rather than chosen by the student)?
Did the classmate's absence of work lead to the group project receiving a failing grade specifically because a required deliverable was never completed?
Did the classmate's assigned portion go undone because the classmate disappeared or was unreachable, leaving the student unable to obtain that portion?
Did the classmate's non-contribution lower the group's score through lost points rather than through an incomplete/failed submission?

Did the classmate's total absence of work mean the group lost the points allotted to that portion, and the sum, averaged over all members, fell below passing, so the student failed despite doing their own part?
Did the classmate's non-contribution leave the group project with a missing section, so the group was assessed a zero on that section, and that zero lowered the overall group score below passing?
Was the group grade determined by the lowest-scoring member (or weakest link), so the classmate's zero or non-work set the group's grade?
Was the group project graded such that the group's score was divided equally among all members, so the student's share of the total points fell below passing because one member contributed nothing?
Was the group project graded as a whole (one shared score for all members), and the classmate's lack of contribution directly reduced that shared score?
Did the student do all of the group's work alone, and did the project still receive a failing score?

Did the student fail the course because they did the entire group project themselves, and the instructor, expecting the work to be split among group members, treated the project as not reflecting the classmate's contribution and penalized the group?
Was the project submitted as a shared group submission that required each member to individually authorize or contribute, and the classmate never did, so the submission was incomplete or failed?
Did the classmate never join or register in the group, so the project counted as submitted by fewer members and the grading was affected (e.g., the group was incomplete)?

Did the student fail because the project was graded on a whole-group basis and the classmate's lack of work meant the group's total score was below the passing threshold, even though the student's own work was excellent?
Was the group's low score due to the classmate's portion being left undone (missing), rather than to incorrect content?
Did the classmate's non-work cause the group to lose points (rather than being rejected or scored zero)?

Did the student fail despite doing excellent work themselves because the group project's shared grade was pulled below passing by the classmate who contributed nothing, and the group grade was what counted toward the student's course grade?
Did the student's excellent individual work not offset the group project failure because the course required a passing grade in the group project component specifically to pass the course?

Did the student fail the course because the group project counted for so much of the grade that its lowered score alone dropped the student's overall average below passing, and this was despite the student excelling in their own individual work?
Did the classmate's lack of work cause the group project to score poorly purely by losing points on the classmate's unworked portion, without any other failing factor?
Did the student knowingly let the classmate free-ride and do nothing, without asking the instructor to reassign or adjust the group?
Were there only two members in the group: the student and the non-contributing classmate?
Did the classmate's non-contribution lower the group score because the project's total possible points included points allocated specifically to the classmate's portion, which were thus lost?

Did the student do their own portion of the group project well, but the classmate did nothing, and the group received a single shared grade that was failing, which caused the student to fail the course despite their own excellent work?
Was the group project grade not literally a shared single score, but the classmate's zero still pulled the student's course grade below passing?

Did the course require each student to individually complete a portion of the group project, and the classmate's zero (no work) directly caused the student's course grade to fall below passing because the group grade was shared?
Was the grading such that the group project's score was computed as the minimum or weakest contribution across members?

Did the classmate's total lack of contribution cause the group project to score below the passing threshold (regardless of exact grading formula), and that failing project score caused the student's course grade to fall below passing?
Did the student personally do all the work for the group project themselves?
Did the student do only their own share of the group project (not the classmate's share), leaving the classmate's assigned part undone?
Given the student did all the work, was the project still graded poorly because the instructor could tell it was done by one person (e.g., the classmate's part was obviously untouched or absent)?

Given the student did all the work, did the classmate's total lack of contribution still cause a low score because the group's grade was shared and averaged over the number of members (so dividing by two with one zero)

Did the classmate's zero on their portion, combined with the student's own portion also being evaluated separately, mean the group's overall score was the average of the student's good score and the classmate's zero?

Was the group project grade computed by splitting the project into individually-assessed parts, where the classmate was assigned a part but produced nothing, so that part scored zero and the group total fell below passing?
Did the student lose points for the classmate's portion being missing because the student was responsible for the overall submission even though the classmate did nothing?
Did the student's failing the course result from a single shared group grade where the group's score — dragged down by the non-contributing classmate — was applied to the student?
Did the student personally do all the work, yet the group grade was dragged down anyway by the classmate's contributing nothing?

Was the classmate's portion of the project physically missing from the final submission (an actual blank or absent section), so the lost points were due to the missing content rather than to grading mechanics like averaging?
Did the student complete the classmate's assigned portion as well, but the group still failed because the grading rubric divided credit per member and the classmate's individual credit was zero?
Did the group fail because the grading rubric required that every member contribute a minimum amount, and the classmate's zero triggered a penalty or failing condition for the whole group?

Did the student do all of the work alone, yet the classmate who did nothing still shared the group's grade, and because the classmate's contribution was zero the shared group grade was poor enough to fail the student?

Was the cause of the low group score that the classmate's share of the work counted as a zero in a shared/averaged grade, rather than because the classmate's portion was left missing from the submitted project?
Did the classmate's unworked portion remain unfilled in the submitted project, and that missing/blank portion caused the group's shared score to fall below passing?
Did the classmate's total lack of contribution trigger a penalty (e.g., group points deducted, docked, or a zero applied) that lowered the shared group grade below passing?

In the shared grading, was the group's project score calculated per member's contribution and set to the lowest individual contribution (so the classmate's zero set the whole group's score to zero or failing)?
Was the group project scored as the average of all members' individual contributions, so the classmate's zero averaged with the student's good score pulled the group below passing?

Did the student, who did all the work alone, still receive the same group grade as the classmate who did nothing, and was that group grade the reason the student failed the course (as opposed to some separate individual requirement)?

The student was excellent at tests and exams, so their individual work would normally earn high marks. This course, however, included a group project worth enough of the course grade that it alone determined pass/fail. The student was placed in a group with a classmate who did literally no work on the project. Because the project received a single shared group grade rather than individually assessed contributions, the classmate's total lack of contribution dragged that shared grade down to a failing level. The failing group-project grade was then applied to the student's course grade — and since the project weight alone was enough to drop the overall average below passing, the student failed the course despite having done all the work alone and excelling in every individual test and exam. Thus a smart student who always passes failed this course because they were graded on a shared group project sabotaged by a non-contributing classmate, not because of any error, illness, cheating, or their own mistake.
Was the classmate's zero rate of contribution specifically the reason the shared group grade fell below passing (as opposed to the student's own work being subpar)?

Did the classmate's lack of contribution cause the group project to fail due to the classmate's portion receiving a zero, rather than because the classmate's absence caused the group to lose some other benefit or requirement?
Did the group project fail primarily because the classmate did not contribute, while the student did their own part?

The student was excellent at individual tests and exams, so their personal work would normally pass easily. This course, however, included a group project weighted heavily enough to determine the course outcome. The student's groupmate — the classmate assigned to the group — did absolutely nothing on the project. Because the project was graded as a single shared group grade rather than by individual contribution, the classmate's total non-contribution dragged the shared project grade down to a failing level. That failing group grade was then applied to the student's course grade, and because the project carried enough weight, it alone pulled the student's overall average below passing. So the smart student who always passes failed the course not through any error, cheating, illness, mistake, or unfair instructor action, but because a non-contributing classmate's zero in a shared group project sank the shared grade to which the student was bound.
